diagnosis: Progress has stalled at polishing the published basin: successive programs return the identical score 0.2087572093785, only $2.85\times10^{-7}$ below the record, with no basin change. Although the tightest $\sim$450 pairs are squeezed within a few $10^{-9}$ with no clear slack gap after a contact shell, the $10^{-9}$ contact graph is highly irregular — hubs with 9–11 contacts, many points with 1–4, and 8 points with zero contacts ("rattlers") whose row-max never attains the global max. The configuration is therefore missing the balanced, near-isostatic structure expected at a strong optimum: every point pinned by roughly 12 contacts with a positive stress equilibrium, every row-max equal to the global max, and a regular contact graph rather than the clustered-plus-isolated-outlier pattern seen in the PCA projection. Because nearly all workers start from the record and accept only immediately-improving LSE/LP steps, kicks either heal back or are rejected, and several over-complex pipelines have crashed or timed out instead of exploring.

diagnosis: Progress has stalled because nearly every successful program starts from the record and returns to the same basin, producing gains of only about \(10^{-10}\) after the initial \(2.85\times10^{-7}\) improvement. The left panel shows a gapless slack spectrum—roughly 140 pairs within \(10^{-9}\) and hundreds more within \(4\times10^{-8}\)—so there is no clean contact set and gradient methods encounter new constraints after extremely small steps. At the plotted threshold the configuration has only about 140 contacts, far below the roughly \(74\cdot12-78=810\) needed to pin the configuration modulo rotations, while contacts per point range from 0 to 11 and seven points are rattlers. The best code is therefore missing a balanced, nearly isostatic contact topology in which load is spread equitably, every point is constrained, and no hub dominates; its clustered, asymmetric contact graph indicates an over-polished descendant of the record rather than a structurally different optimum.
